title: Danville School District to adopt locked phone pouches - NewsBreak
text: DANVILLE, Ill. (WCIA) — The Danville School District is trying to get students to put their phones down. The School Board met Tuesday night and approved a new measure that will keep students in tune with their teachers. Danville High School and North Ridge Middle School will adopt Yondr pouches — gray pockets that lock phones away for the entire school day. High School Principal Jacob Bretz said it took officials, including himself, a lot of time to get on board with the idea. He said it’s something they thought about implementing years ago in a limited capacity, but that Yondr takes a more all or nothing approach. Bretz knows not everyone will be on board with that philosophy, but he thinks it’s the best decision to ultimately help students learn without distraction. “While it’s going to be hard and it’s going to be a big shift, I wouldn’t be doing my job if I didn’t try to do something about [phone usage],” Bretz said. “I think this is the best way because it’s cut and dry, it’s black and white. There’s no wiggle room; there’s no gray area.” Students will be able to stay in contact with parents throughout the day via email on school-issued computers. All in all, the pouches will cost $70,000 — almost $43,000 for the high school and $27,000 for the middle school. Students will be required to use the pouches this upcoming school year.
